title: A/R Detail: ID sorts by number value, and ties go by number
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Make sure that in the "1-30 days past due" bucket there are three open invoices with the same due date, document A, document B and document C, whose numbers have different digit counts, so that in number order they read document A, document B, document C but in letter-by-letter order document B, document C, document A.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Detail (Reports, then "A/R Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
  • Leave the report with the "1-30 days past due" bucket expanded.
  • If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Click the "ID" header.
  2. Click the "ID" header again.
  3. Click the "Due Date" header.
  4. Click the "Due Date" header again.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Rows inside each aging bucket sort by ID as numbers, never letter by letter, smallest number first: document A, document B, document C.

Step 2:

  • Largest number first: document C, document B, document A, still in number order.

Step 3:

  • Rows inside each aging bucket sort by Due Date, oldest first.
  • Document A, document B and document C tie on Due Date, so they are ordered by number, smallest first: document A, document B, document C.

Step 4:

  • The Due Date sort reverses, newest first.
  • The three still tie and keep the same order, smallest number first: document A, document B, document C (reversing a sort reverses the sorted column only).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 9 (23 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 26 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11532 (Story 2, Sort by clicking any column header)

  • S2-R4: “ID and No. sort by number value: S1-99 before S1-100 before S1-101. The first click puts the smallest number first and the second click the largest first. The same number-aware order breaks ties in every sort, always smallest document number first: reversing a sort reverses the sorted column only, so tied rows keep that order in both directions. A date column compares the day only, never the time of day, so two rows on the same date are a tie.”
  • S2-R1, A/R Detail columns: “A/R Detail: Date, Location (when shown), Transaction Type, ID, Customer Full Name, Due Date, Amount, Open Balance.”
  • S2-R2: “The first click gives the useful order for the kind of data: text (names, Location, Transaction Type) A to Z; money columns largest first; dates oldest first; Past Due largest first; ID and No. smallest number first (S2-R4). The second click reverses it. The third click repeats the first; there is no unsorted state.”
